title: Progressive, flat and regressive taxes
examples: Why is a sales tax called regressive?

explain.say: Should someone who earns a lot pay a bigger share of income in tax than someone who earns a little? Countries answer differently. Look at the board: a line showing the share of income paid in tax, rising as income rises. That is a progressive tax.

See the marks? In this example, low earners pay nothing, middle earners 20 percent on part of their income, and high earners 40 percent on the top part. Each slice, called a band, has its own rate. India, Japan and the UK all use bands. Why might people support that?

Now a regressive tax, where the share falls as income rises. Imagine a fixed tax of 10 on every phone. For someone earning 100, that is 10 percent; for someone earning 1,000, just 1 percent. Look at the falling line. Who feels it more?

Some countries use a flat tax, one rate for everyone, like 10 percent in Bulgaria. Look at both sides: flat is simple; progressive asks more from those who earn more. Which feels fairer to you? Thoughtful people disagree.
So the shape of the line shows who carries the load. Superb thinking! Wow: Bulgaria's flat income tax is just 10 percent, while Japan's top national rate is 45 percent, with a local tax on top.

faq.a: A progressive tax takes a bigger share of income from people who earn more, usually by charging higher rates on higher slices of income.
A regressive tax takes a bigger share of income from people who earn less. A fixed charge, or a sales tax on everyday goods, often works this way.
asks: Why is a sales tax regressive?

faq.a: A flat tax charges everyone the same rate, such as 10 percent, whatever they earn. Bulgaria and Estonia use flat income taxes.
asks: Which countries have a flat tax?

faq.a: A tax band is a slice of income with its own rate. Only the money inside a higher band is taxed at the higher rate, not your whole income.
It depends on your view of fairness. Some say everyone should pay the same rate; others say those who earn more can afford to pay a bigger share. Most countries mix systems.

facts: Bulgaria has a flat personal income tax of 10 percent.
Japan's top national income tax rate is 45 percent, plus a local inhabitant tax of about 10 percent.

quiz.say: A fixed tax of 10 on a phone. What share of income is it for someone earning 100?
quiz.show: A fixed tax of 10 on a phone. What share of income is it for someone earning 100?

wrong.0: 1 percent is the share for someone earning 1,000.
wrong.2: That would mean the tax took all their income.

quiz.say: In a progressive system, what happens to the tax rate on extra income as income rises?
quiz.show: In a progressive system, what happens to the tax rate on extra income as income rises?
quiz.why: Higher slices of income are taxed at higher rates.

wrong.1: A falling share describes a regressive tax.
wrong.2: The same rate for everyone is a flat tax.
